result.summary: Logs the symlink-resolved canonical path of the active data directory during node startup logging. The resolved path is printed unconditionally on a separate line immediately following the configured data directory line.
result.problem: When the data directory or its parent paths contain symlinks, startup logs only print the configured path. Users and developers analyzing saved debug.log files cannot verify the actual underlying storage device or directory used during that run.
evidence: Author description: 'I've been testing a potential performance PR across different data directories (for example, SSD versus HDD). After each run, I save the debug.log file. It would be nice if the debug.log file showed which data directory was used for that run.'

Author description: 'If a script starts bitcoind (e.g., on an RPi with a whole infrastructure, like Umbrel or myNode), changing the startup command arguments may be inconvenient or not even possible. It's easy to change the default directory to be a symlink. But in that case, debug.log doesn't show where the actual data directory is located.'
result.changed_since_previous: The new version unconditionally logs the 'Resolved data directory' line on every startup instead of only printing it when the canonical path differs from the configured path, ensuring log parsers can rely on the line being present.
result.card: Logs the symlink-resolved canonical data directory during node startup immediately after the configured path. This makes saved debug.log files reflect the physical storage directory used when running bitcoind via symlinked paths. The author notes this assists benchmarking across different storage media when wrapper scripts prevent modifying startup flags. No dependencies.

risk.why: Touches only startup logging using standard filesystem canonicalization with an error code fallback.
